question: In standard nursing research, when is a result considered statistically significant?

options.A: When the null hypothesis is proven to be 100% true
options.B: When the p-value is greater than 0.50
options.C: When the sample size is larger than the population
options.D: When the p-value is less than or equal to 0.05

explanation: Awesome! A p-value of 0.05 or less means there's a 5% or lower chance your results happened by luck. That's our green light for significance! [learn more](GNS217_U4_T3#GNS217_U4_T3_h4)

question: Which tiny, hair-like parts of the respiratory tract get paralyzed and destroyed by cigarette smoke?

options.A: Cilia
options.B: Alveoli
options.C: Bronchioles
options.D: Pleura

explanation: Cilia are the tiny sweeping brushes of the lungs that clear out mucus and dirt. Smoke damages them badly, but understanding this puts you one step ahead! [learn more](GNS313_U3_T5#GNS313_U3_T5_h3)

question: Which type of stretcher splits into two halves so you can slide it under a patient without rolling them?

options.A: Scoop stretcher
options.B: Basket stretcher
options.C: Canvas folding stretcher
options.D: Rigid spine board

explanation: Spot on! A scoop stretcher splits lengthwise, making it super helpful when you want to avoid rolling a fragile patient. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T10#GNS112_U7_T10_h4)

question: Besides hands-on technical procedures, what major professional skill is greatly improved through simulation teamwork?

options.A: Effective communication and team coordination
options.B: Advanced medical billing and coding
options.C: Hospital accounting and financial budgeting
options.D: Maintenance of hospital medical equipment

explanation: Simulation scenarios require students to talk clearly, assign roles, and work together as a cohesive healthcare unit. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T8#GNS212_U4_T8_h3)

question: What is the medical term for a severe infection located right inside the bone tissue?

options.A: Nonunion
options.B: Compartment syndrome
options.C: Avascular necrosis
options.D: Osteomyelitis

explanation: Osteo means bone, and myelitis refers to the marrow/infection. Put them together, and you get osteomyelitis—a stubborn bone infection that needs aggressive treatment. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T23#GNS222_U1_T23_h6)

question: Your clinic has limited funds and staff. How should you decide which health problem to tackle first?

options.A: Prioritize based on urgency, severity, and feasibility of intervention
options.B: Choose whichever problem is easiest to ignore until next year
options.C: Let a coin flip decide which program receives funding
options.D: Select the problem that costs the most money to fix

explanation: Resources are always tight, so smart nurses target problems that are urgent, severe, and actually possible to fix with the resources on hand. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T8#GNS124_U3_T8_h5)

question: Why must nurses and doctors strictly avoid inserting fingers into the vagina (digital exam) when placenta praevia is suspected?

options.A: It will immediately cause the baby to drop into a breech position
options.B: It introduces severe bacterial infection into the amniotic sac
options.C: It can disrupt the placenta and trigger massive, life-threatening bleeding
options.D: It causes the uterine muscle to contract into painful spasms

explanation: Touching the lower segment through the vagina can tear the low-lying placenta and cause severe hemorrhage. Knowing this safety rule keeps mothers safe! [learn more](GNS226_U2_T017#GNS226_U2_T017_h3)

question: Why are nurses well-positioned to advocate for food policy changes?

options.A: They are primarily responsible for writing national agricultural laws
options.B: They witness the direct health impacts of poor nutrition in clinical practice
options.C: They control the financial budgets of international food agencies
options.D: They manage the commercial distribution of imported grain

explanation: Nurses see malnutrition and diet-related disease daily, giving them firsthand evidence of policy needs. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T028#GNS227_U2_T028_h8)

question: Why are there 8 pairs of cervical (neck) nerves when there are only 7 cervical vertebrae?

options.A: The eighth nerve originates from the upper thoracic section of the spinal cord
options.B: The cervical spine contains an extra hidden vertebra that houses the eighth nerve
options.C: The first cervical nerve exits above the first vertebra, and the eighth exits below the seventh vertebra
options.D: Cervical nerves divide into two branches as they leave the spinal cord

explanation: Don't let this trick you! Because the first seven nerves exit above their matching vertebrae, an extra eighth nerve sneaks out below the seventh vertebra to bridge us into the chest area. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T26#GNS211_U3_T26_h1)

question: Which food texture is safest for a patient with severe swallowing difficulties and missing teeth?

options.A: Regular solid
options.B: Raw vegetables
options.C: Pureed
options.D: Mechanically soft

explanation: Pureed foods are smooth and need zero chewing effort, making them much safer and easier for a struggling patient to swallow. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T7#GNS112_U5_T7_h5)

question: When is a line graph preferred over a bar chart in clinical data presentation?

options.A: When comparing completely separate hospital departments
options.B: When tracking continuous changes over a period of time
options.C: When counting nominal categories like blood types
options.D: When showing proportions of a whole budget

explanation: Line graphs are designed for sequential, continuous data like hourly vitals, whereas bar charts show separate categories. [learn more](GNS217_U4_T7#GNS217_U4_T7_h4)

question: Why does pelvic inflammatory disease (PID) raise a woman's risk of having an ectopic pregnancy?

options.A: Hormonal imbalances stop the uterine lining from growing
options.B: Scar tissue blocks and damages the fallopian tubes
options.C: Infection prevents the ovaries from releasing eggs
options.D: Bacteria destroy the muscular walls of the uterus

explanation: When PID heals, it leaves behind scar tissue that narrows the tubes. If a fertilized egg gets stuck in that narrow, scarred tube, it implants right there instead of the uterus. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T12#GNS311_U1_T12_h5)

question: Why is infection control still necessary in a quarantine zone where people are initially well?

options.A: To replace the need for daily temperature checks
options.B: To eliminate all bacteria from the human body permanently
options.C: To ensure that health workers do not need to wear masks
options.D: To prevent healthy residents from catching the infection from each other

explanation: If one person in quarantine is incubating the virus, poor hygiene can easily spread it to others in the same facility. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T5#GNS313_U2_T5_h5)

question: Which major complication is a well-known risk for patients taking long-term NSAIDs (like ibuprofen)?

options.A: Gastrointestinal bleeding
options.B: Rapid bone lengthening
options.C: Severe permanent blindness
options.D: Excessive red blood cell production

explanation: NSAIDs can irritate the stomach lining because they block protective substances called prostaglandins. That's why patients often take them with food or stomach protectors! [learn more](GNS222_U1_T12#GNS222_U1_T12_h8)

question: What is the main reason teenagers often avoid seeking healthcare for sensitive personal issues?

options.A: Preference for traditional herbal remedies only
options.B: Fear of parents or community members finding out
options.C: A lack of interest in personal hygiene
options.D: The high cost of prescription eyeglasses

explanation: Without guaranteed privacy, teens worry about gossip and judgment from adults they know in the community. Privacy builds trust! [learn more](GNS312_U3_T18#GNS312_U3_T18_h3)

question: Which ethical principle are you upholding when you give a patient honest, complete details about a drug's side effects?

options.A: Maleficence
options.B: Paternalism
options.C: Autonomy
options.D: Fidelity

explanation: Spot on! Autonomy is all about respecting the patient's right to make their own choices based on honest and clear information. [learn more](GNS215_U2_T3#GNS215_U2_T3_h7)

question: Which of these does NOT help reduce sampling error in a research project?

options.A: Applying proper random sampling techniques during selection
options.B: Reducing the overall sample size to make data collection faster
options.C: Using a well-calculated and sufficiently large sample size
options.D: Ensuring the sampling frame covers the entire target population

explanation: Correct! Shrinking your sample size actually makes sampling errors worse, not better. Bigger, well-chosen samples are more reliable. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T18#GNS224_U1_T18_h6)

question: Which type of larvae is mainly responsible for causing myiasis (infestation of tissue) in humans?

options.A: Moth caterpillars
options.B: Dipterous fly larvae
options.C: Aquatic mosquito larvae
options.D: Seed tick arachnids

explanation: Flies from the Diptera order lay eggs that hatch into maggots, which can feed on human tissue and cause myiasis. You're building solid clinical instincts! [learn more](GST114_U3_T7#GST114_U3_T7_h2)

question: What is the proper way to position an adult's ear before putting in ear drops?

options.A: Pull the pinna up and back before instilling the drops
options.B: Keep the client sitting upright for thirty minutes after
options.C: Insert the dropper tip firmly deep into the ear canal
options.D: Pull the earlobe straight down before putting in drops

explanation: Correct! Pulling the pinna up and back opens up the canal so the drops slide right down nicely toward the eardrum. [learn more](GNS311_U3_T7#GNS311_U3_T7_h6)

question: What is the main idea behind the 'One Health' approach to disease control?

options.A: Focusing solely on human hospital care during a disease outbreak
options.B: Treating every infectious disease with a single universal antibiotic
options.C: Eliminating all wild animals to protect human settlements entirely
options.D: The interconnected health of humans, animals, and the environment

explanation: One Health reminds us that human health is tied to the health of our animals and our shared environment. We have to look at the big picture! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T94#GNS214_U1_T94_h4)

question: What would happen to the accessory sex glands if a man's testosterone levels dropped very low?

options.A: They would shrink and decrease their secretions
options.B: They would grow larger and produce excess fluid
options.C: They would immediately start producing female hormones
options.D: They would convert into urinary storage tissues

explanation: Without adequate testosterone support, these accessory organs atrophy and their secretory output drops. [learn more](GNS121_U4_T3#GNS121_U4_T3_h6)

question: Which lab test is commonly ordered first when checking for an autoimmune disorder?

options.A: Blood culture and sensitivity
options.B: Fast blood glucose
options.C: Antinuclear Antibody (ANA) test
options.D: Complete blood count without differential

explanation: The ANA test checks for antibodies that attack the nucleus of your own cells. It's a very common early screening tool for autoimmune conditions like lupus. [learn more](GST114_U4_T7#GST114_U4_T7_h6)

question: What is an important way community health nurses can help prevent FGM?

options.A: Performing mild forms of FGM under hygienic conditions
options.B: Issuing legal certificates permitting traditional circumcisers
options.C: Subsidizing the cost of traditional ceremonies
options.D: Educating local communities about the health risks of FGM

explanation: Spot on! Community health nurses play a huge role in prevention by raising awareness and teaching families about the dangers of FGM. Brilliant work today! [learn more](GNS225_U6_T2#GNS225_U6_T2_h8)

question: Why must a nurse pay attention to workplace hazards even if they currently feel strong and healthy?

options.A: Because infectious diseases disappear once they are identified
options.B: Because patients expect nurses to know about building safety
options.C: Because early awareness prevents future injury and chronic illness
options.D: Because hospital laws require passing a test every month

explanation: Many workplace risks cause slow, quiet damage over years of practice. Knowing the dangers now keeps you protected down the road. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T7#GNS122_U3_T7_h1)

question: Through which structure must a flatus tube pass to enter the rectum?

options.A: The anal sphincters
options.B: The pyloric sphincter
options.C: The duodenal ampulla
options.D: The ileocecal valve

explanation: To enter the rectum safely, the tube needs to pass through the internal and external anal sphincters. You've got this! [learn more](GNS212_U1_T11#GNS212_U1_T11_h1)

question: What is the very first step in how cancer starts in the body?

options.A: Chronic dehydration of body tissues
options.B: Excessive intake of dietary proteins
options.C: Rapid spread of bacteria in the blood
options.D: Genetic mutation in a single cell

explanation: Cancer kicks off when a change happens in a cell's genes, making it grow and divide without stopping. You've got this! [learn more](GNS321_U1_T4#GNS321_U1_T4_h1)

question: What is the main purpose of the blood-testis barrier created by Sertoli cells?

options.A: To filter out excess water from the seminal fluid
options.B: To prevent the immune system from attacking developing sperm cells
options.C: To stop bacteria from traveling upward from the urinary tract
options.D: To maintain high blood pressure inside the seminiferous tubules

explanation: Because developing sperm have unique proteins, the blood-testis barrier shields them from being attacked by white blood cells. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T7#GNS216_U2_T7_h5)

question: What is the medical term for the uterus shrinking back to its normal size after birth?

options.A: Exfoliation
options.B: Lactation
options.C: Autolysis
options.D: Involution

explanation: Great job! Involution is just the word we use for the uterus shrinking back down to its pre-pregnant size. Think of it like a rubber band slowly returning to its original shape. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T013#GNS226_U3_T013_h2)

question: Which of the following is NOT a reason why nurses must follow strict infection control during an epidemic?

options.A: To prevent the nurse from contracting the infectious agent
options.B: To protect other vulnerable patients admitted to the ward
options.C: To stop the hospital environment from spreading the disease
options.D: To guarantee that patients pay their hospital bills on time

explanation: Brilliant! Infection control is entirely about safety and stopping the spread of germs, and has nothing to do with hospital bills or payments. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T15#GNS313_U1_T15_h8)

question: What is the general relationship between calcium and phosphate in our blood?

options.A: They always rise and fall together at the same time
options.B: They generally move in opposite directions
options.C: They both depend entirely on daily sodium intake
options.D: They have no chemical or physiological connection

explanation: Think of them like a seesaw! In the blood, when calcium goes up, phosphate usually goes down. You're doing great learning these dynamics. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T11#GNS121_U2_T11_h3)

question: A patient with an advanced illness is physically stable, but their family looks completely exhausted and anxious. What should you do as the nurse?

options.A: Ask the doctor to discharge the patient immediately to relieve stress
options.B: Tell the family to go home and rest until the patient's condition worsens
options.C: Focus only on the patient since their physical vitals are stable
options.D: Include the family's coping capacity as part of your ongoing assessment

explanation: When the family is worn out, it affects the patient too! Checking in on how the family is coping is a vital part of good nursing care. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T4#GNS321_U4_T4_h2)

question: Which serious lung condition is a major emergency for a pregnant woman with sickle cell disease?

options.A: Placental abruption
options.B: Hyperemesis gravidarum
options.C: Acute chest syndrome
options.D: Gestational diabetes

explanation: Spot on! Acute chest syndrome involves lung infection and tissue damage, bringing chest pain and fever that needs fast medical care. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T005#GNS226_U4_T005_h2)

question: What factor do you look at during a socio-economic and environmental nutritional check?

options.A: Basal energy expenditure measured in a laboratory
options.B: Ability to afford, access, and safely prepare food
options.C: Exact microscopic cellular enzyme activity levels
options.D: Genetic predisposition to inherited metabolic diseases

explanation: Socio-economic checks look at the real-world picture: can they afford food, get to a market, and cook it safely? [learn more](GNS124_U6_T5#GNS124_U6_T5_h5)

question: Why do diagnostic tools in primary health care need to be simple and affordable?

options.A: Laboratory tests are always completely inaccurate
options.B: Primary care centers have limited resources and high community needs
options.C: Nurses are not allowed to use expensive equipment
options.D: Patients in rural communities rarely get sick

explanation: Primary health care serves everyday people with tight budgets, so we need accessible and cost-effective tools that work well in our local clinics. Great job thinking practically! [learn more](GNS124_U6_T4#GNS124_U6_T4_h1)

question: Why is maternal mortality still high in many parts of Nigeria?

options.A: Infectious diseases have been completely wiped out
options.B: Pregnant women completely refuse to visit healthcare facilities
options.C: Transport delays, money issues, and a shortage of skilled staff
options.D: There are too many modern hospitals in remote villages

explanation: You've got this! A mix of delayed care-seeking, poor roads and transport, and health system gaps contributes heavily to poor maternal health outcomes in Nigeria. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T004#GNS226_U1_T004_h1)

question: What is the only true cure for preeclampsia?

options.A: Complete bed rest
options.B: High-dose vitamin tablets
options.C: Delivery of the placenta
options.D: Cutting out salt completely

explanation: Because preeclampsia originates from the placenta, bringing the baby and the placenta out into the world is the only way to fully stop the condition. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T019#GNS226_U2_T019_h5)

question: What is the primary role of the subthalamus?

options.A: Processing the sense of smell and taste
options.B: Regulating the production of red blood cells
options.C: Producing hormones to control blood pressure
options.D: Coordinating smooth skeletal muscle movements

explanation: Spot on! The subthalamus teams up with the basal ganglia to make sure your body movements are smooth and controlled. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T19#GNS211_U3_T19_h5)

question: How do local farmers directly support school feeding initiatives?

options.A: By teaching science classes on agricultural botany
options.B: By prescribing nutritional supplements to sick children
options.C: By supplying locally grown, nutritious food produce
options.D: By auditing the financial books of the school canteen

explanation: Local farmers provide fresh food ingredients, ensuring the feeding program is sustainable and utilizes local produce. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T6#GNS225_U4_T6_h6)

question: What happens to a drug revolving fund over time if free drugs are given out but never paid for by a subsidy?

options.A: The pharmacy inventory will steadily deplete and collapse
options.B: The government will automatically double its funding
options.C: The fund will grow larger and more profitable
options.D: Drug manufacturers will begin supplying free items forever

explanation: Remember, a revolving fund depends on money returning when drugs are sold. If stock is given away without a replacement fund, the pharmacy will soon run out of cash to restock. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T6#GNS215_U3_T6_h5)

question: What is a practical, budget-friendly nursing tip for a patient who cannot afford fresh vegetables?

options.A: Advise them to forage for wild plants in local public parks
options.B: Telling them to skip vegetables entirely until they find more money
options.C: Suggesting nutritious frozen vegetables or rinsed canned options
options.D: Insisting they only buy organic produce from specialty markets

explanation: Well done! Frozen and canned veggies are affordable, last longer, and still offer great nutrition when money is tight. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T010#GNS227_U7_T010_h7)

question: A senior doctor frequently interrupts junior nurses and dominates a committee meeting. What is the best action for the chairperson to take?

options.A: Ask the junior nurses to leave the room until the discussion ends
options.B: Politely acknowledge the input and redirect the floor to quieter participants
options.C: Ignore the behavior so the senior doctor does not get offended
options.D: Cancel all future committee meetings to avoid conflict

explanation: A great chair handles dominant speakers respectfully while making space for everyone else to share. [learn more](GST321_U7_T4#GST321_U7_T4_h7)

question: Which of the following is considered a microvascular complication of chronic diabetes?

options.A: Peripheral vascular claudication pain
options.B: Severe hypertension from aortic stenosis
options.C: Coronary artery disease and stroke
options.D: Diabetic retinopathy and nephropathy

explanation: Microvascular complications involve damage to small blood vessels, specifically harming the eyes (retinopathy) and the kidneys (nephropathy). [learn more](GNS222_U2_T8#GNS222_U2_T8_h7)

question: A hospital ward plan fails the moment a sudden influx of accident victims arrives. What was missing from this plan?

options.A: Necessary flexibility and backup procedures
options.B: Too much focus on patient education
options.C: Input from doctors instead of experienced nurses
options.D: Goals that were far too ambitious and expensive

explanation: A plan that breaks during an emergency lacks the adaptability required in fast-paced healthcare settings. [learn more](GST321_U1_T7#GST321_U1_T7_h4)

question: Why should parents praise a gifted child's hard work rather than their raw smarts?

options.A: To prevent the development of crippling perfectionism
options.B: To speed up asynchronous physical growth rates
options.C: To eliminate the need for specialized schooling
options.D: To guarantee university admission later in life

explanation: Praising effort teaches kids that it's okay to make mistakes and try again. Praising 'smartness' can make them terrified of failing later on. Beautiful learning moment! [learn more](GNS225_U5_T1#GNS225_U5_T1_h5)

question: What is the main idea behind situational leadership?

options.A: Every nurse manager should use an autocratic style
options.B: Only transformational leaders succeed in healthcare
options.C: Leadership style never changes regardless of the task
options.D: Leaders must adapt their style to the context and staff

explanation: Situational leadership requires changing how you lead based on the needs of the staff and the situation at hand. [learn more](GST321_U3_T3#GST321_U3_T3_h6)

question: What does the 'Great Man' theory say about leadership?

options.A: Leadership qualities are inherited at birth
options.B: Anyone can learn to lead through weekend workshops
options.C: Only senior physicians are capable of guiding ward staff
options.D: Leadership depends entirely on the surrounding environment

explanation: The Great Man theory suggests that great leaders are born with natural talents, rather than trained. A bit old-school, but an important concept to know! [learn more](GST321_U3_T2#GST321_U3_T2_h2)

question: Why is it helpful to feel (palpate) the patient's lower belly before doing a catheterisation?

options.A: To stimulate the urethral sphincter to open
options.B: To check if the kidneys are infected
options.C: To measure the exact length of the urethra
options.D: To confirm the presence of a full, distended bladder

explanation: Spot on! Feeling the lower belly (suprapubic area) lets you check if urine is actually backed up and trapped in the bladder, confirming you really need to catheterize. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T20#GNS212_U1_T20_h5)

question: Why is collecting health data but never analyzing or using it considered a bad practice?

options.A: It automatically invalidates all future requests for international donor grants
options.B: It violates international copyright laws regarding health registers
options.C: It wastes valuable time and resources while failing to improve community health outcomes
options.D: It causes immediate supply chain shortages in urban pharmacies

explanation: Collecting data takes hard work from nurses and patients. If no one looks at it to make decisions, that effort goes to waste! [learn more](GNS225_U2_T21#GNS225_U2_T21_h6)

question: What is the main reason young children experience so many domestic accidents?

options.A: Lack of proper formal education in school
options.B: A deliberate desire to break household rules
options.C: An inherited weakness in motor coordination
options.D: Natural curiosity combined with unsafe surroundings

explanation: Children love to explore their world! When dangerous items are left within their reach, accidents can easily happen. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T12#GNS313_U3_T12_h3)

question: When giving a bed bath, in what direction should you wash the skin?

options.A: From the feet up to the face
options.B: From dirtiest areas to cleanest areas
options.C: From the left side to the right side
options.D: From cleanest areas to dirtier areas

explanation: Brilliant! Moving from clean to dirty ensures you don't drag germs from lower areas up onto sensitive spots like the face. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T2#GNS324_U6_T2_h3)

question: As a nurse, what is your most important duty when caring for an elderly patient with severe osteoporosis?

options.A: Applying continuous heavy traction to strengthen weak leg bones
options.B: Restricting dietary calcium intake to prevent mineral crystal buildup
options.C: Implementing strict fall prevention protocols in the environment
options.D: Encouraging complete bed rest to prevent accidental bone trauma

explanation: Prevention is key! Keeping the environment safe from slips and trips protects fragile bones from breaking. Excellent nursing care! [learn more](GNS121_U3_T4#GNS121_U3_T4_h8)

question: Which data collection method involves talking directly with trusted village leaders about local health issues?

options.A: Laboratory blood screenings
options.B: Key informant interviews
options.C: Direct environmental observation
options.D: Reviewing census registers

explanation: Key informants are knowledgeable community figures who provide deep insight into local health behaviors and needs. [learn more](GNS313_U4_T1#GNS313_U4_T1_h3)

question: What is a major sign of a high bowel blockage like a duodenal obstruction?

options.A: Inability to pass flatus
options.B: Bright red rectal bleeding
options.C: Frequent projectile vomiting
options.D: Watery diarrhea with mucus

explanation: Spot on! When the upper digestive tract is blocked, food and fluids have nowhere to go but back up, leading to frequent vomiting of stomach contents. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T7#GNS213_U3_T7_h3)

question: If an endotracheal tube advances too far down the trachea, which mainstem bronchus does it most commonly enter?

options.A: The right mainstem bronchus
options.B: It enters both mainstems equally
options.C: It stops directly at the carina
options.D: The left mainstem bronchus

explanation: The right main bronchus has a wider and more vertical angle, making it much easier for a deep tube to slip into it by mistake. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T16#GNS213_U2_T16_h7)

question: Which of these is an indigenous fruit commonly found in Nigerian local markets?

options.A: African star apple (agbalumo)
options.B: Imported green kiwi fruit
options.C: Fresh arctic cloudberries
options.D: Temperated climate wild blueberries

explanation: Correct! Agbalumo is a beloved seasonal Nigerian fruit packed with wonderful vitamins and fiber. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T010#GNS227_U4_T010_h5)

question: A patient with high blood pressure and high blood sugar is told to switch from white bread to whole grain bread. Why is this a great choice?

options.A: Refined white bread has no calories for the body to process
options.B: Whole grains retain fiber, which slows digestion and prevents sharp sugar spikes
options.C: Whole grains eliminate all fats from the patient's daily diet
options.D: Whole grains contain complete proteins that repair damaged blood vessels

explanation: You nailed it! The natural fiber in whole grains slows down how fast sugar enters the blood, keeping levels nice and steady. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T004#GNS227_U4_T004_h2)

question: In the ABCDE primary survey, what does the letter 'D' stand for?

options.A: Disability
options.B: Diagnosis
options.C: Drainage
options.D: Dehydration

explanation: D is for Disability! It is just a quick check of the patient's neurological status and brain function. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T2#GNS321_U2_T2_h2)

question: Before the treaty, why did companies love to ship toxic waste to other countries?

options.A: Shipping companies received government tax breaks for exports
options.B: Developing nations had weak laws and lower disposal costs
options.C: Poorer countries urgently needed industrial ash for road building
options.D: Developing nations specifically requested toxic chemicals for farming

explanation: Exactly! Safe waste disposal is expensive. Companies saved money by taking advantage of countries that didn't yet have strict environmental laws. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T18#GNS122_U3_T18_h2)

question: What is the main goal of sex therapy when treating sexual dysfunction?

options.A: Treating underlying bacterial infections
options.B: Replacing surgical and pharmacological treatments entirely
options.C: Lowering blood pressure and heart rate instantly
options.D: Reducing performance anxiety and improving communication

explanation: You got it! Sex therapy is all about taking off the pressure, easing anxiety, and helping partners talk openly about their feelings. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T24#GNS312_U1_T24_h7)

question: Before a solid pill can cross into the bloodstream, what must happen to it first?

options.A: It must pass through the kidneys first
options.B: It must reach the large intestine intact
options.C: It must combine with red blood cells
options.D: It must disintegrate and dissolve in fluids

explanation: Solid medicine can't just slip through cell walls as a hard chunk. It has to break apart and completely dissolve in fluid first! [learn more](GNS125_U3_T4#GNS125_U3_T4_h3)

question: What is the name of the primary law protecting persons with disabilities in Nigeria?

options.A: The Discrimination against Persons with Disabilities Act
options.B: The Public Infrastructure and Welfare Decree
options.C: The Nigerian Social Services and Rehabilitation Law

question: How does lacking formal education directly impact a girl's future health?

question: What fluid mainly fills the hollow chambers (ventricles) inside the brain?

question: What is the internationally recognized age below which a union is considered child marriage?

question: A student gets severe eye strain and sleepiness during afternoon lectures in a room with no windows. What is the most likely physical cause?

question: What is the best way for doctors to find out exactly which germ is causing a newborn's eye infection?

question: Why must nurses work alongside community leaders when trying to stop breast ironing?

question: Why is interpersonal communication considered the gold standard for changing health behaviour?

explanation: Spot on! Continuing professional development (CPD) ensures we keep learning and sharpening our skills throughout our careers. [learn more](GST321_U8_T7#GST321_U8_T7_h4)

question: Roughly how much does a normal, full-term placenta weigh?

options.A: 100 grams
options.B: 1000 grams
options.C: 500 grams
options.D: 250 grams

explanation: Think of it as about 500g—roughly one-sixth of the baby's birth weight! Knowing this helps you spot when a placenta is unusually small or heavy. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T5#GNS121_U6_T5_h1)

question: A patient is reading a food label and asks which line is most important for managing their diabetes. What should the nurse point out?

options.A: Total carbohydrates
options.B: Total sodium
options.C: Total calories
options.D: Total protein

explanation: Total carbohydrates have the biggest impact on blood glucose, making it the most critical number on the label for diabetes management. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T012#GNS227_U6_T012_h6)

question: What is a core public health strategy used to manage HIV here in Nigeria?

options.A: Quarantining all infected individuals in remote camps
options.B: Banning the import of foreign foods
options.C: Expanding access to Antiretroviral Therapy (ART)
options.D: Treating all patients with high-dose antibiotics only

question: What is the main purpose of gentle stretching exercises in degenerative disorders?

options.A: To cure underlying nerve damage
options.B: To increase overall bone length
options.C: To reverse muscle wasting completely
options.D: To prevent painful joint contractures

explanation: Gentle stretching keeps joints flexible and helps stop the painful tightening of muscles and tendons known as contractures. You are mastering this! [learn more](GNS222_U4_T17#GNS222_U4_T17_h4)

question: What does a null hypothesis usually state?

options.A: There is a strong positive effect from the treatment
options.B: There is no relationship between the variables
options.C: The sample size is too small to complete the study
options.D: The research question was poorly written

explanation: The null hypothesis is the 'no difference' or 'no effect' guess. It assumes any change you see is just by chance! [learn more](GNS217_U3_T10#GNS217_U3_T10_h3)

question: Which common health condition is most directly managed by cutting down on salty foods?

options.A: Osteoporosis
options.B: Hypertension
options.C: Iron deficiency anemia
options.D: Type 1 Diabetes

explanation: Spot on! Too much salt makes the body hold onto water, driving up blood pressure. Lowering sodium is key for our patients with hypertension. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T003#GNS227_U7_T003_h4)

question: What is the main goal of giving birth control counseling during Post-Abortion Care (PAC)?

options.A: To prevent repeat unintended pregnancies and subsequent unsafe abortions
options.B: To enforce government population control quotas in rural areas
options.C: To punish the patient for engaging in premarital sex
options.D: To permanently sterilize high-risk young women

explanation: PAC counseling is all about empowering women with choices so they can protect their health and avoid future unplanned pregnancies. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T003#GNS226_U5_T003_h8)

question: You hear a call bell ring, but right at that moment, another patient starts struggling to breathe. What should you do first?

options.A: Finish charting at the desk before responding to either
options.B: Assess the patient who is struggling to breathe
options.C: Answer the call bell immediately to find out what is needed
options.D: Ask a visitor to check on the patient in the room

explanation: Brilliant! ABC comes first. A breathing difficulty is a life-threatening emergency that always beats a general call bell. [learn more](GST321_U4_T4#GST321_U4_T4_h4)

question: A 25-year-old male client reports finding a hard, painless lump in his left testicle. What should the nurse suspect first?

options.A: Prostate adenocarcinoma
options.B: Testicular cancer
options.C: Benign prostatic hyperplasia
options.D: Renal cell carcinoma

explanation: Testicular cancer is most commonly seen in young adult men. A painless lump or swelling in the scrotum should always be checked out right away. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T9#GNS213_U4_T9_h4)

question: How do alkylating agents mainly damage cancer cells?

options.A: By replacing normal cell wall lipids
options.B: By cross-linking DNA strands to stop replication
options.C: By stimulating rapid immune responses
options.D: By blocking plant-derived microtubules

explanation: You're doing great! Alkylating agents tie up the DNA strands so they cannot pull apart and copy themselves, stopping the cancer from spreading. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T7#GNS215_U6_T7_h2)

question: What are the earliest vital sign clues that a patient might be bleeding internally after a biopsy?

options.A: Sudden high blood pressure and a very slow pulse
options.B: Falling blood pressure and a fast heart rate
options.C: Rising fever and flushed skin
options.D: Slow, deep breathing with high oxygen levels

explanation: Spot on! When blood is lost inside, blood volume drops. The heart beats faster to make up for it, while blood pressure starts to slide down. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T10#GNS221_U2_T10_h5)

question: Why must you check a patient's kidney function before they get an injection of contrast dye?

options.A: Contrast dye increases the daily urine output significantly
options.B: Poor kidney function prevents the dye from reaching the joints
options.C: Kidneys must filter the dye to make bones show up white
options.D: Contrast dye can be toxic to the kidneys if clearance is slow

explanation: The kidneys have to filter out contrast dye. If a patient's kidneys aren't working well, the dye can linger and cause kidney damage, so checking lab results first is a crucial nursing duty. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T4#GNS222_U1_T4_h7)

question: What is the main goal of cancer rehabilitation?

options.A: Curing the primary cancer diagnosis
options.B: Preventing the recurrence of tumors
options.C: Managing acute surgical site infections
options.D: Restoring physical and emotional well-being

explanation: You got this! Cancer rehab is all about helping patients get back their strength, independence, and good quality of life after treatment. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T11#GNS321_U1_T11_h1)

question: Who is a key partner in sustaining school health initiatives within the local area?

options.A: Commercial advertising agencies
options.B: Foreign manufacturing industries
options.C: International sports federations only
options.D: The Parent-Teacher Association (PTA)

explanation: PTAs connect the school with parents and community members who provide vital support and resources for health projects. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T3#GNS225_U4_T3_h7)

question: Why do most nurses love using the formula method for drug calculations?

options.A: It is a straightforward, reliable way to figure out the required dose
options.B: It automatically converts pounds to kilograms without math
options.C: It eliminates the need to ever verify orders with the pharmacist
options.D: It works exclusively for intravenous medications

explanation: You got it! The 'Desired over Have' formula gives you a clear, easy-to-remember shortcut for your daily clinical math. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T6#GNS125_U2_T6_h1)

question: How do nursing theorists define 'health' within our professional framework?

options.A: A dynamic state of physical, mental, and social well-being
options.B: The complete elimination of all hospital admissions nationwide
options.C: The total absence of any identifiable bacteria in the blood
options.D: A static condition achieved strictly through pharmaceutical drugs

explanation: Health isn't just the literal absence of sickness. In nursing, we see it as a flowing, everyday state of overall physical, mental, and social well-being. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T1#GNS112_U1_T1_h4)

question: When a patient experiences a permanent sensory loss, what emotional and psychological response do nurses frequently need to help them manage?

options.A: Grief, social withdrawal, and depression
options.B: Severe memory loss and confusion about time
options.C: Aggression and physical violence toward staff
options.D: Euphoria and unrealistic optimism about recovery

explanation: Losing sight or hearing is a massive life change. Patients often go through a grieving process and might pull away from others, so our empathetic nursing support is crucial here. [learn more](GNS311_U3_T9#GNS311_U3_T9_h4)

question: Why is even a small, subtle change in one body system so risky for a critically ill patient?

options.A: It can quickly lead to multi-organ collapse and emergency
options.B: It only affects the specific organ without causing other issues
options.C: It means lab values are completely normal
options.D: It usually indicates that the patient is ready for discharge

explanation: Think of it like a house of cards—very sick patients have little backup energy, so a small glitch can rapidly cascade into a bigger emergency. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T1#GNS221_U4_T1_h1)

question: What triggers the baby's circulatory system to close its fetal blood shunts?

options.A: Putting eye ointment in
options.B: Changes in oxygen levels and clamping the cord
options.C: The vernix washing away
options.D: Brown fat kicking in

explanation: When the cord is clamped and the baby takes that first big breath, oxygen levels change in the chest, telling those temporary fetal shunts to close up. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T011#GNS226_U1_T011_h5)

question: A patient with an underactive thyroid gland will most likely show which sign?

options.A: Changes in energy levels and metabolism
options.B: Rapid spikes in calcium-regulating hormones
options.C: Severe trouble controlling blood sugar
options.D: Holding onto too much water with very little urine

explanation: That's right! The thyroid controls your body's engine speed, so when it slows down, the patient often feels sluggish and tired. [learn more](GNS211_U1_T1#GNS211_U1_T1_h3)

question: A patient has heavy postpartum bleeding and a soft, boggy uterus. What should you do first?

options.A: Prepare the patient for an immediate MRI scan
options.B: Encourage the patient to walk around the ward
options.C: Perform bimanual uterine massage
options.D: Insert a nasogastric tube for decompression

explanation: Massaging the uterus helps the muscle contract tightly, which closes off bleeding blood vessels. Great nursing intervention! [learn more](GNS226_U1_T009#GNS226_U1_T009_h6)

question: How does keeping a community clean and sanitary help stop the spread of disease using the epidemiological triangle?

options.A: It alters the environment to prevent agent-host contact
options.B: It permanently alters the immune system of the host
options.C: It transforms a viral agent into a harmless bacterium
options.D: It directly destroys the genetic material of the agent

explanation: Great thinking! Good sanitation changes the environment so germs have a much harder time traveling from their source to a human host. [learn more](GST114_U2_T5#GST114_U2_T5_h1)

question: What are the three fundamental pillars that drive population dynamics?

options.A: Agriculture, industry, and commerce
options.B: Fertility, mortality, and migration
options.C: Taxation, inflation, and employment
options.D: Housing, transport, and electricity

explanation: Think of these three as the core of demography: births (fertility), deaths (mortality), and people moving around (migration). They tell the whole story of how a population changes! [learn more](GNS226_U6_T007#GNS226_U6_T007_h3)

question: What is your immediate action if the patient feels sharp pain while you are flushing their ear?

options.A: Push the syringe faster to clear the blockage
options.B: Lower the temperature of the water
options.C: Stop the irrigation procedure right away
options.D: Ask the patient to lie flat on the bed

question: Why is early identification of genetic risks important for nurses in primary healthcare?

options.A: It prevents patients from developing infectious diseases
options.B: It allows for proactive education and early risk reduction
options.C: It completely cures the genetic condition before birth
options.D: It eliminates the need for any further medical testing

explanation: Spotting risks early gives healthcare providers the chance to guide families and prevent severe complications before symptoms appear. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T15#GNS311_U1_T15_h1)

question: Why do lung problems often affect the rest of the body?

options.A: Lung infections spread directly to the brain within hours
options.B: Every organ relies heavily on a steady supply of oxygen from the lungs
options.C: Poor breathing causes the stomach to stop digesting food completely
options.D: The heart stops pumping blood when the lungs become inflamed

explanation: You got it! If the lungs aren't working well, oxygen delivery drops, and every single tissue in the body starts to suffer. Oxygen is food for our cells! [learn more](GNS213_U2_T12#GNS213_U2_T12_h1)

question: Why is it important for nurses to understand that inherited degenerative disorders are progressive?

options.A: It allows nurses to completely cure the disease using specialized medications
options.B: It guarantees that symptoms will appear immediately at birth
options.C: It helps nurses anticipate and plan for the patient's future care needs
options.D: It proves the illness was caused by a recent environmental exposure

explanation: Because these conditions worsen over time, knowing their trajectory helps nurses prepare patients and families for upcoming physical and cognitive changes. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T20#GNS222_U4_T20_h1)

question: What is a dangerous storage practice that often leads to accidental poisoning?

options.A: Using weekly pill boxes for daily vitamins
options.B: Keeping medicines in a locked bathroom cabinet

options.D: Putting cleaning chemicals in old beverage bottles

question: Why do families in traditional societies sometimes continue the practice of early marriage?

options.A: Because schools refuse to educate unmarried teenagers

options.C: Because modern laws actively mandate early marriage for population growth
options.D: Because it is deeply rooted in generational customs and community expectations

question: Which finding is considered a normal, expected temporary side effect following a cystoscopy procedure?

options.B: Inability to feel the need to urinate for several weeks
options.C: Severe lower abdominal pain radiating to the shoulders
options.D: Complete absence of urine output for twenty-four hours

question: Why is a 'just culture'—where nurses can report mistakes without fear of punishment—so important?

options.A: It removes all legal liability from the hospital organization
options.B: It encourages honest reporting of mistakes so systemic flaws can be fixed
options.C: It ensures that negligent staff members never face disciplinary action
options.D: It eliminates the need for incident report documentation

explanation: A just culture focuses on fixing broken systems rather than just blaming individuals. When people aren't terrified to speak up, everyone learns and patients stay safer! [learn more](GST321_U1_T14#GST321_U1_T14_h7)

question: What is the main reason a nurse performs a follow-up check after giving medication?

options.A: To ask the patient to sign the hospital billing forms

options.C: To remind the doctor when the next shift starts
options.D: To clean up the leftover water cups from the bedside table

explanation: Follow-up monitoring ensures therapeutic effectiveness and catches early signs of adverse reactions. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T14#GNS122_U1_T14_h7)

question: What is the main purpose of the evaluation step in the nursing process?

options.C: To administer emergency medications during a crisis
options.D: To determine if the patient met the established care goals

question: Why shouldn't a nurse rely only on visual physical checks when diagnosing malnutrition?

question: Which of these items is a classic biological hazard you'll encounter on the wards?

options.D: Expired non-prescription tablets

question: Which of the following is NOT a standard immediate action when caring for a patient in shock?

options.A: Providing high-flow oxygen

options.C: Establishing large-bore IV access
options.D: Applying warm blankets

question: What is the nurse's main role when it comes to informed consent?

options.A: Writing the medical prescription for the diagnostic procedure

options.C: Deciding whether the patient is well enough to undergo the test
options.D: Ensuring the patient understands the procedure and has signed voluntarily

explanation: Well done! The nurse makes sure the patient truly gets what the doctor explained and is agreeing of their own free will—no pressure! [learn more](GNS311_U1_T5#GNS311_U1_T5_h2)

question: What is the main thing sedative medications do to the body?

options.A: Increased skeletal muscle contraction
options.B: Central nervous system depression
options.C: Enhanced sensory perception
options.D: Central nervous system stimulation

question: Why is it important for researchers to discuss study limitations during data interpretation?

options.A: To prove that their research is completely flawless and superior
options.B: To justify increasing the budget for future research projects
options.C: To confuse readers so they do not question the findings
options.D: To honestly acknowledge any weaknesses or factors that could affect the results

explanation: No study is perfect, and transparency about limitations builds scientific credibility. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T1#GNS217_U3_T1_h6)

question: What is the main goal of using the TNM staging system for lung cancer?

options.C: To calculate the patient's exact daily calorie requirements
options.D: To identify which specific type of cigarette the patient smoked

question: When do symptoms of neonatal tetanus usually first show up?

question: Why do theatres use smoke evacuation systems during surgeries that involve burning or cutting tissue with electrical devices?

options.A: To keep the operating room temperature from rising too high

options.C: To remove toxic smoke plumes and viral particles from the air
options.D: To prevent the fire alarm system from going off in the hospital

question: How do remote monitoring devices help a home nurse care for a heart failure patient?

options.A: By replacing the need for physical nursing visits entirely throughout the year

options.C: By automatically administering emergency intravenous cardiac medications without human input
options.D: By transmitting daily weight and vital signs remotely to catch worsening fluid retention early

explanation: Remote gadgets let nurses track daily stats so they can spot danger signs and step in before it turns into a hospital emergency. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T2#GNS324_U1_T2_h5)

question: What diagnostic procedure involves placing small amounts of suspected allergens on the back under tape for 48 hours?

options.A: Wood's light exam
options.B: Patch testing
options.C: Skin scraping
options.D: Punch biopsy

question: What happens when Cooper's ligaments stretch or lose their elasticity?

question: Which group of symptoms strongly points towards preeclampsia in a pregnant patient?

options.C: High blood pressure, headache, and visual disturbances
options.D: Lower back pain and increased appetite

question: What is a major challenge that often stops clients from completing a family planning referral?

question: Why do patients in areas with few clinics feel extra pressured to stay quiet?

options.A: They receive free private insurance coverage

options.C: They have few alternative clinics to go to if they are mistreated
options.D: They are legally forbidden from speaking to nurses

question: What is the main goal of laws like the Violence Against Persons Prohibition (VAPP) Act regarding FGM?

options.A: To provide financial grants to families who continue the tradition

options.C: To force hospitals to perform FGM under sterile conditions

question: What does a demographic rate typically measure?

options.D: How often an event happens in a population over time

question: Which medical protection is mandatory for all nursing students and staff before starting clinical duties?

options.D: Hepatitis B vaccination

question: How would you best describe a 'geopolitical' community?

options.A: A religious group meeting across multiple countries

question: What is the recommended approach for routine daily care of a normal umbilical cord stump?

options.C: Keeping it clean, dry, and exposed to air

question: How is the pathway of our sense of smell (olfaction) different from all other senses?

options.C: It crosses over to the opposite side of the brain twice

question: Why is the family considered a primary unit of care in palliative care?

options.C: They experience the burden of illness and need support too.
options.D: They make all medical decisions without the patient.

explanation: Because a serious illness affects the entire family unit, palliative care extends support to relatives during the illness and through bereavement. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T1#GNS321_U4_T1_h2)

question: What are the three main building blocks of healthcare financing?

options.C: Budgeting, staffing, and facility management
options.D: Patient admission, treatment, and discharge

question: Why would a doctor choose skeletal traction over skin traction for a broken femur?

options.C: It allows much heavier weights to be used safely
options.D: It permits the patient to walk around the ward freely

question: Which type of range of motion exercise requires the patient to move their own joints to build strength?

options.C: Passive range of motion
options.D: Static stretching motion

question: Where is milk actually manufactured inside the breast?

options.B: Adipose cells

options.D: Alveoli

question: What does the term 'intervention fidelity' mean in community nursing?

options.C: Ensuring community members trust the local nursing staff
options.D: Securing loyal financial donors for long-term health projects

question: Which body system does your skin belong to?

options.B: The respiratory system

question: Which of the following is NOT a focus area during a health inspection survey in an SNF?

question: If you are posted as a nurse to a new displacement camp, what major environmental challenge should you expect?

options.B: Excessive availability of modern private housing
options.C: Complete absence of any communicable diseases
options.D: Overcrowding and limited access to clean water

question: Why is it super important to check if a research study is valid before using its findings on your hospital ward?

options.C: To prevent using flawed ideas that could harm patients

question: What skill must a good nursing leader have alongside management abilities?

question: How should you respond if a client worries that injectable contraceptives cause permanent infertility?

options.B: Tell the client to ignore her worries and take the medication anyway
options.C: Refuse to give her any more supplies until she stops asking questions
options.D: Agree that fertility is permanently destroyed after one injection

question: An elderly client living alone cannot walk well enough to go to the local market. What community resource can you suggest?

question: What does the nutrition acronym RDA stand for?

question: What is the most reliable way to monitor a patient's response to a high calorie diet over time?

question: Why can severe, untreated constipation sometimes lead to a fecal impaction?

options.D: Excess water floods the intestines and washes away all waste

question: A patient suddenly starts wheezing, develops hives, and has facial swelling ten minutes after an injection. What should you do right away?

options.A: Tell the client to walk home quickly and rest in bed
options.B: Wait another hour to see if the symptoms disappear on their own
options.C: Administer intramuscular epinephrine and monitor vital signs
options.D: Document the mild local reaction and send the client away

explanation: These are classic signs of anaphylaxis. Quick action with intramuscular epinephrine can prevent the airway from closing up. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T73#GNS214_U1_T73_h8)

question: Which group of hospitalized individuals faces the highest risk for severe falls?

options.A: Older adult patients
options.B: Visiting family members
options.C: Young pediatric infants
options.D: Night shift desk nurses

explanation: Aging bodies often experience muscle weakness, balance issues, and dizziness from medications, making older adults much more vulnerable to falls. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T7#GNS112_U4_T7_h4)

question: What is the main purpose of giving a patient a purgative?

options.A: To increase the absorption of water in the large intestine
options.B: To slow down gastrointestinal motility and prevent diarrhea
options.C: To promote bowel movements and relieve constipation
options.D: To neutralize excess stomach acid and soothe ulcers

explanation: You've got this! Purgatives are simply given to help clear the bowels and get things moving when a patient is constipated. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T2#GNS223_U3_T2_h1)

question: What is the main trigger for releasing secretin from the small intestine?

options.D: The sight and smell of favorite foods

explanation: Secretin is released when stomach acid arrives, telling the pancreas to send out bicarbonate to neutralize it. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T11#GNS121_U1_T11_h7)

question: What is the name for that blood-tinged mucus plug that drops when the cervix starts opening up?

options.A: The show
options.B: Lightening

options.D: Amniotic fluid

explanation: We call it 'the show'! It's a classic early sign that the cervix is getting ready and opening up for labour. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T002#GNS226_U3_T002_h2)

question: How do a person's cultural and spiritual beliefs usually affect how they grieve?

options.A: They shape the expected rituals and public ways of mourning
options.B: They stop family members from feeling anticipatory grief
options.C: They shorten the time a person feels sad
options.D: They completely take away all anger and sadness

explanation: Culture and religion give people a comforting framework, ceremonies, and traditions to help guide them through loss. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T6#GNS221_U4_T6_h5)

question: During which phase of adolescence do teenagers really start thinking deeply and caring a lot about what their friends think?

options.A: Late adolescence
options.B: Early adolescence

question: What is a common emotional response a patient might experience after an abortion?

options.A: An immediate desire to write a public memoir about the event
options.B: Complete emotional numbness that lasts for an entire lifetime
options.C: A wide range of feelings including relief, grief, or anxiety
options.D: Permanent clinical detachment from all family members

explanation: Exactly! Feelings after pregnancy loss are deeply personal and can span anywhere from sadness and anxiety to relief. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T006#GNS226_U5_T006_h4)

question: Why do laws requiring parental consent for minor treatments often harm adolescent health?

options.A: They prevent nurses from administering routine childhood immunizations
options.B: They discourage adolescents from seeking care for sensitive issues out of fear
options.C: They cause doctors to refuse treatment for routine malaria and fevers
options.D: They make clinic waiting times much longer for everyone in the community

explanation: When teens know their parents must be informed, they often avoid seeking vital care for reproductive health or substance use. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T16#GNS312_U3_T16_h4)

question: A nurse manager wants to graph staff numbers across four units: ICU, Emergency, Pediatrics, and Surgery. Which chart fits best?

options.A: A bar chart, because the departments are separate categories
options.B: A scatter plot, because departments change over time
options.C: A pie chart showing only the ICU department
options.D: A histogram, because staff counts are continuous numbers

explanation: Because these hospital units are distinct, separate groups rather than a continuous scale, a bar chart is the right tool. [learn more](GNS217_U4_T9#GNS217_U4_T9_h3)

question: What is the very first thing you should do if you accidentally get a needle stick injury?

options.B: Squeeze the finger to drain as much blood as possible
options.C: Wash the affected area immediately with soap and water
options.D: Apply an antibiotic ointment and a bandage

question: Why do some communities continue to practice FGM across generations?

options.A: Local religious texts explicitly command the surgery
options.B: Modern scientific journals endorse the procedure
options.C: It is viewed as a vital cultural rite of passage
options.D: Government health laws strongly mandate the practice

question: Why is empowering women through education considered a key objective within population policies?

options.A: It ensures women never participate in agricultural activities.
options.B: It forces families to move permanently to urban centers.
options.C: It eliminates the need for any maternal healthcare clinics.
options.D: It naturally influences family size choices and improves overall health.

explanation: Education is a game-changer! When women are educated, they often choose to marry a bit later, seek out better healthcare, and freely decide on family sizes that work best for them. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T007#GNS226_U6_T007_h2)

question: How does the constant push for a male child indirectly cause higher rates of dangerous bleeding after birth?

options.A: It forces pregnant women to avoid attending antenatal care clinics entirely
options.B: It causes surgical instruments used during delivery to become contaminated
options.C: It restricts mothers from eating iron-rich foods after giving birth

question: Which quick screening tool is specifically designed to check for substance use risks in teenagers?

question: In health science, what does the term 'sex' actually refer to?

options.D: Biological and physiological differences

question: A nurse wants to teach mothers how to prevent severe dehydration from watery stools in infants. What should be the main demonstration?

options.C: How to completely stop the baby from drinking fluids
options.D: How to perform emergency intravenous surgery

explanation: Teaching mothers home preparation of oral rehydration solution saves lives by treating early fluid loss before it becomes critical. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T4#GNS124_U1_T4_h2)

question: Why is preventing hypothermia especially important in a severely injured trauma patient?

options.C: Cold body temperatures can interfere with normal blood clotting
options.D: Hypothermia stops the patient from feeling any physical pain

question: What exactly is caregiver burnout?

question: What chemical trigger makes the ductus arteriosus close up after birth?

question: Which drug is given as the specific antidote for a severe paracetamol (acetaminophen) overdose?

question: Which type of medication is commonly prescribed to ease painful muscle stiffness and spasms?

question: What is a direct positive outcome of strong teamwork in a hospital?

question: Why are pregnant women more prone to developing urinary tract infections?

question: What is a great way for a father to support the mother after childbirth?

question: Which tool is used to hold the surgical needle securely when repairing an episiotomy?

question: A patient eating a full liquid diet after surgery suddenly gets severe stomach cramps and vomits. What should you do first?

question: Why must community health nurses work closely with WASH (Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene) teams in an IDP camp?

question: What is one of the primary frontline duties of a community health nurse during an outbreak?

question: If a patient is taking Ethambutol, what regular assessment should you prioritize?

question: Which of the following is NOT a common cause of inaccurate pulse oximeter readings?

question: Which of these is NOT a good step when setting up a clean workspace on a household table?

question: How does human relations theory change the daily role of a nurse manager?

question: Which of these is a major nitrogen waste product that the placenta clears away from the baby?

question: What is required before giving any medication authorized by a standing order?

question: You are helping a patient with severe bradykinesia get ready in the morning. What is the best nursing action?

question: Why do midwives and doctors check red blood cell indices (like MCV) in an anemic pregnant woman?

question: Why is building trust through compassionate nursing care important in reproductive health?

question: How does team nursing differ from total patient care?

question: A nutrient crosses the intestinal lining with the help of a carrier protein, moving down its concentration gradient without using ATP. What is this called?

question: Why do doctors check thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) and prolactin when investigating missed periods?

options.C: They confirm whether the patient has an anatomical outflow blockage

question: Why is self-awareness so important for a nurse leader?

options.C: It helps them recognize their own emotional triggers and clinical limits.

explanation: Knowing your own strengths and where you might need help stops overconfidence and helps you keep your emotions in check during stressful moments on the ward. [learn more](GST321_U3_T4#GST321_U3_T4_h2)

question: Why does the timing of certain reproductive health tests matter so much?

question: Why is a low white blood cell count (neutropenia) a medical emergency for patients on chemotherapy?

options.D: It causes immediate, uncontrollable bleeding from small skin cuts

question: Which cells in your body carry MHC Class I molecules on their surface?

question: What is the most common medication given sublingually for sudden chest pain?

question: What is the medical name often used for andropause?

question: What is an example of community mobilization in primary health care?

question: What is a major clinical benefit when a husband knows basic pregnancy danger signs?

question: What is the primary target site for medication administered via the intrathecal route?

question: Why does blood pressure fall in early and mid-pregnancy even though blood volume is rising?

options.B: The heart pumps with much less force
options.C: Blood vessels constrict to push blood to the lungs
options.D: Progesterone reduces systemic vascular resistance

question: During the extension movement, what part of the baby's face sweeps out of the vagina first?

question: What do the letters in the SBAR communication tool stand for?

question: A patient with a degenerative condition frequently becomes exhausted halfway through a morning walk. What physical therapy strategy should be introduced?

question: Which substance must be present in a rehydration solution to help activate the SGLT1 transporter in the gut?

question: Which of these is NOT a safe safety practice in the operating room?

question: What must you always check before involving a partner or family member in a PAC patient's care plan?

options.D: Proof of legal marriage verified by hospital registration
